newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria tells EU to change posture or face review.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria tells EU to change posture or face review.

text.p: Nigeria's military government on Friday deplored what it called the unfriendly posture of the 15-member European Union countries towards it and urged them to change or face a review of relations.

The government's number two Lieutnant-General Oladipo Diya addressed ambassadors and representatives of EU countries in the capital Abuja where he accused them of boycotting major events of the administration, the News Agency of Nigeria reported.
"In the circumstance, our government may, in the same vein and in our national interest, be compelled to review social and economic relations with the EU," Diya said.
Relations between Nigeria and Western governments have been unsteady since 1993 when the a previous army government annulled a presidential poll to restore democracy.
They worsened last November when the military authorities defied worldwide appeals for clemency and hanged writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight minority rights activists for murder.

The EU like the United States slammed a wide range of sanctions including on the sale of arms, a freeze of aid, boycott of sporting contacts and visa restrictions on members of the military government and their families.
Few ambassadors attended the meeting in Abuja.
Nigeria's military authorities, under fire abuse for alleged human rights abuses and lack of democracy, have set a transition plan to return the country to civilian rule by October 1998.
